subject: Re: Hosted API — Volume slabs, model premiums, and commit mechanics
messages:
From: Lilly Tran <lilly.tran@stately.ai>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@stately.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing questions and commit structure

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — great context. Our procurement and finance teams have two follow-ups before we can move to a PO:

1) We run both generation-heavy chat (customer-facing) and high-volume embeddings for semantic search. Can you confirm how the per-token discounts apply across model families? Specifically: are embeddings priced as a separate meter with separate slabs, or do they count toward the same commit?

2) We saw mention of a "model premium" for larger LLMs. For planning purposes, can you provide the multiplier or explicit $/1k-token rates for the premium chat model vs standard? We need numbers we can put in our TCO spreadsheet.

3) Commit mechanics: Stately prefers a 12-month ramped commit (quarterly checkpoints) rather than a single large up-front committal. Are quarterly ramp schedules supported, and can unused commit in one quarter roll forward?

If you can share a simple worksheet outlining slab breaks and model multipliers, that would help speed approvals.

Thank you — copying procurement (procurement@stately.ai) for visibility.

Lilly
Lilly Tran
Head of Platform Operations | Stately AI
Attachment: (none)

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
To: Lilly Tran <lilly.tran@stately.ai>
Cc: procurement@stately.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 17:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing questions and commit structure

Hi Lilly — really glad the demo was useful. Quick answers up front and I'll follow with a worksheet in the next email: 

- Embeddings: billed on a separate meter and counted separately for slab calculations (so embeddings volume does not automatically offset chat usage). We can, however, offer a blended slab for committed blended volume if Stately prefers one invoice line — that is a negotiable concession.

- Model premiums: we typically apply a model multiplier on top of the base chat rate. Example multipliers: standard chat = 1.0x, large-premium chat = 1.8x–2.2x depending on context (latency SLO and quantization). Embeddings are priced from a different base (lower per-token unit) but can have a smaller premium for highest-accuracy embed models (e.g., 1.3x). I'll send tabulated $/1k-token examples.

- Commit mechanics: we support ramp schedules and quarterly checkpoints. By default unused committed tokens do not roll forward, but we can include a 12-week rollover window or convert unused commit to credits at an agreed % if you need that.

I'll loop in Sean to share the worksheet and a draft SOW.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing questions and commit structure

Hi Lilly — attaching a simple worksheet and a draft SOW to make the numbers concrete. Below is the proposed structure we discussed internally. Numbers are illustrative; final pricing will be in the SOW/contract.

Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Tiers_v3.xlsx (xlsx, 72KB)
Attachment: SOW-Stately-Draft.docx (docx, 28KB)

Proposed commercial summary (12-month term):
- Base chat rate (standard models): $0.60 / 1k prompt+completion tokens
- Premium chat model multiplier: 2.0x (-> $1.20 / 1k tokens); applies to model SKUs marked PREMIUM in the catalog
- Embeddings base: $0.12 / 1k embedding tokens
- High-accuracy embedding model premium: 1.35x (-> $0.162 / 1k)

Volume slabs (chat and embeddings are separate meters by default):
- 0–50M tokens / month: list pricing (no discount)
- 50M–250M tokens / month: 10% discount off list
- 250M–1B tokens / month: 22% discount off list
- 1B+ tokens / month: custom enterprise slab (we generally bring this to sales ops)

Optional blended commit (if Stately wants a single committed dollar/token pool covering both chat+embeds):
- We can offer blended slabs where combined usage qualifies for higher discounts; in that case we calculate an effective blended base and apply per-model multipliers. Example: a blended 250M token commit could shift the effective discount to ~25% because embeddings volume is cheaper.

Commit mechanics and ramp:
- Accept quarter-by-quarter ramp (e.g., Q1 = 20% of annual commit, Q2 = 30%, Q3 = 25%, Q4 = 25%).
- Unused commit: default is no roll-forward. Option A: 12-week rollover window. Option B: convert unused commit to platform credits at 60% of list value (to be used for overage or next quarter).

Other notes:
- We can include a one-time onboarding credit (usually $10–25k) for pilots to defray early overage risk.
- SLA-tiered pricing: if you require the 99.95% latency SLA and dedicated capacity, premium multiplier may increase ~10–15% to account for reserved capacity.

Next steps: if the structure looks reasonable, we can (1) agree on blended vs separate meter, (2) pick a ramp schedule, and (3) I'll push a redlined SOW and PO-ready pricing.

Thanks — looping Marissa (commercial ops) and Connor (legal) for SOW and contract items.

—Sean Gallagher
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Sean / Tessa — thanks for the clear worksheet and options. Procurement is comfortable with the proposed quarterly ramp and the 12-week rollover (Option A). A few clarifications before we sign: 

- Can you cap the premium multiplier to 2.0x guaranteed for the term (we want predictability even if you add newer SKUs)?
- For blended commit, would you accept a blended invoice line but still break out consumption per meter for billing visibility? That would work best for our FP&A.
- For onboarding credit: can Stately get the $20k onboarding credit in the first invoice as an invoice-level credit (not a future-service credit)?

If you can confirm the above in a revised SOW, procurement will prepare a PO and sign. Please also include the HubSpot deal link on the SOW for reconciliation.

Lilly
Lilly Tran
Head of Platform Operations | Stately AI
procurement@stately.ai
